'''Denzel Mahoney''' (born January 18, 1998) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton Bluejays]] and the [[Southeast Missouri State Redhawks men's basketball|Southeast Missouri State Redhawks]].

==High school career==
Mahoney attended [[Paul J. Hagerty High School]] in [[Oviedo, Florida]]. He was named Florida 8A State Player of the Year as a junior.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Saverino |first1=Nate |title=Two-Minute Drill: Denzel Mahoney Named "Freshman of the Week" |url=https://www.krcu.org/post/two-minute-drill-denzel-mahoney-named-freshman-week#stream/0 |website=[[KRCU]] |access-date=December 30, 2020 |date=January 19, 2017}}</ref> He suffered a torn ACL during an [[Amateur Athletic Union]] game and missed his senior season while rehabilitating. Mahoney committed to playing college basketball for [[Southeast Missouri State Redhawks men's basketball|Southeast Missouri State]].<ref name="pfeifer">{{cite web |last1=Pfeifer |first1=Ben |title=Blocking out the Silence: Denzel Mahoney thrives on malleability |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2020/05/29/blocking-out-the-silence-denzel-mahoney-thrives-on-malleability/ |website=The Rookie Wire |access-date=December 30, 2020 |date=May 29, 2020}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman at Southeast Missouri State, Mahoney averaged 14.9 points per game and earned [[Ohio Valley Conference]] (OVC) Freshman of the Year honors and a spot on the all-OVC second team. He followed this up by raising his scoring average to 19.3 points per game in his second season and garnered first-team All-OVC accolades.<ref>{{cite news|title =Mahoney and Brewer Earn All-OVC Accolades|url= https://gosoutheast.com/news/2018/2/27/mens-basketball-mahoney-and-brewer-earn-all-ovc-accolades.aspx|date=February 27, 2018|website=gosoutheast.com|accessdate=December 20, 2020}}</ref> Following his sophomore season, Mahoney transferred from the Redhawks, ultimately settling on [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Gordon|first=Jeff|title= SEMO's Ray among the many mid-major coaches facing talent raids|url= https://www.stltoday.com/sports/columns/jeff-gordon/gordo-semos-ray-among-the-many-mid-major-coaches-facing-talent-raids/article_4e5d5146-21f2-542f-ac2b-3bacee8e042d.html |date=May 29, 2018|website=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]]|accessdate=December 20, 2020}}</ref>

After transferring, Mahoney sat out the 2018–19 season per [[NCAA]] rules. He became eligible on December 17 the following season. He led all [[Big East Conference]] non-starters in scoring at 12 points per game and received the Big East [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Sixth Man of the Year|Sixth Man of the Year]] award.<ref>{{cite news|last=Nyatawa|first=Jon|title= Creighton's Denzel Mahoney named Big East sixth man of the year |url= https://omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/creighton-s-denzel-mahoney-named-big-east-sixth-man-of-the-year/article_6469f0b8-263a-5dea-a43e-b7d668399394.html|date=March 9, 2020|website=[[Omaha World-Herald]]|accessdate=December 20, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title= Denzel Mahoney Earns BIG EAST's Sixth Man Award|url= https://gocreighton.com/news/2020/3/9/mens-basketball-denzel-mahoney-earns-big-easts-sixth-man-award.aspx|date=March 9, 2020|website=gocreighton.com|accessdate=December 20, 2020}}</ref> Following the season, Mahoney declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]], but ultimately returned for his final season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Creighton backup Denzel Mahoney declaring for NBA draft|url= https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29045247/creighton-backup-denzel-mahoney-declaring-nba-draft|date=April 16, 2020|website=[[ESPN.com]]|accessdate=December 20, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Nyatawa|first=Jon|title= Denzel Mahoney, Damien Jefferson withdrawing from NBA draft, returning to Creighton|url= https://omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/denzel-mahoney-damien-jefferson-withdrawing-from-nba-draft-returning-to-creighton/article_448fa869-23ba-5d39-87de-e857e5b58dbd.html|date=August 1, 2020|website=[[Omaha World-Herald]]|accessdate=December 20, 2020}}</ref> As a senior, he averaged 12.5 points and 4.1 rebounds per game. Mahoney declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his final season of eligibility that was granted by the NCAA due to the COVID-19 pandemic.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Nyatawa |first1=Jon |title=Creighton's Denzel Mahoney won't return for extra season |url=https://omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/creightons-denzel-mahoney-wont-return-for-extra-season/article_b53cf50a-9635-11eb-bb93-ffea1f6083dc.html |access-date=June 22, 2021 |work=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |date=April 16, 2021}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Austin Spurs (2021–2023)===
After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Mahoney joined the [[Charlotte Hornets]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Hornets Announce Roster For MGM Resort NBA Summer League 2021|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/hornets-announce-roster-mgm-resort-nba-summer-league-2021|website=NBA.com|date=August 2, 2021|access-date=August 2, 2021}}</ref> and on October 6, 2021, he signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Jeff|last=Garcia|title=Spurs ink guard Denzel Mahoney to an Exhibit 10 deal|url=https://www.kens5.com/article/sports/nba/spurs/spurs-guard-denzel-mahoney-exhibit-10-deal-nba-san-antonio/273-1e87b7b5-1197-4915-9570-96eaefb756e0|work=KENS5|date=October 6, 2021|access-date=October 8, 2021}}</ref> However, he was cut from training camp before opening night.<ref>{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Spurs Cut Jaylen Morris, Denzel Mahoney; Will Sign Jordan Burns|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/10/spurs-cut-jaylen-morris-denzel-mahoney-will-sign-jordan-burns.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 11, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}}</ref> On October 27, he signed with the [[Austin Spurs]] as an affiliate player.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Austin Spurs|title=Our 2021-22 training camp roster is set!|number=1453389119367925764|user=austin_spurs|date=October 27, 2021|access-date=October 31, 2021}}</ref>

On October 28, 2023, the [[Iowa Wolves]] selected Mahoney with the 57th pick in the [[2023 NBA G League draft]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Iowa Wolves Select Three Players in 2023 NBA G League Draft|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/iowa-wolves-select-three-players-in-2023-nba-g-league-draft/n-6026625|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 28, 2023|access-date=November 4, 2023}}</ref> However, they waived him on November 8.<ref>{{cite news|title=2023-2024 Iowa Wolves Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Iowa-Wolves/4/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 6, 2023}}</ref>
